provenance: Spec-authored with msgpack-python 1.2.4 (str keys in schema order, use_bin_type). Not yet a C# capture: the first conformance PR for each runtime re-captures these with its own encoder and the bytes must match, as error-vectors.json does. Every schema case is checked against cultnet.write-admitted.schema.json / cultnet.error.v1.schema.json in this directory.

message.error: write_not_authorized: the catalog refused the document
message_invalid: the message could not be read
message_invalid: the message could not be read
limit_reached: the session's remembered-write limit is full

blankFields.semantics: A put whose document 'names nothing' is refused like a frame that does not read (error.v1 message_invalid, details.field "message", the write's id, the fixed text of error_v1_empty_schema_id_is_unreadable_and_names_the_write) and never applied, on every connection, receipt-capable or not. Each case starts from this valid document: schemaId note.v0, recordKey note:1, storedAt 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z, payload 81A16101 (hex), no source ids, no tags; 'set' replaces or adds the named fields. A blank string is empty or made only of Unicode White_Space code points (the list in whiteSpaceCodePoints, the PropList property, the same in every runtime; U+200B, U+FEFF, U+180E and U+001C to U+001F are not White_Space, though some platforms' whitespace tests accept some of them). Fields not listed are valid. 'unset' means the key is absent or nil, which is not blank: those cases are admitted.
blankFields.codePointCases: For every code point in whiteSpaceCodePoints, each of schemaId, recordKey, storedAt, sourceRuntimeId, sourceAgentId, sourceRole and one tags entry, set alone to a string of just that code point (and to that code point repeated three times), is refused; for every code point in notWhiteSpaceCodePoints the same string is not blank and the put is admitted.

admittedMessageId.semantics: Decoder-side rule for a `cultnet.write_admitted.v0` frame's `messageId` (Heimdall's ruling, write-receipt.md). Valid only if it contains at least one Unicode letter (\p{L}) or number (\p{N}) AND no Default_Ignorable_Code_Point (DerivedCoreProperties). The compare is RAW: the id is echoed byte for byte, so a decoder neither trims nor normalizes. Each case's id is given as `codePoints` (hex, in order), repeated `repeat` times (default 1), so no lone surrogate appears in this file. A runner builds the frame {schemaVersion write_admitted.v0, messageId, operation put, schemaId note.v0, recordKey note:1} with its own encoder and decodes it with the write_admitted decoder; `refuse` means the decoder refuses the frame the way it refuses an empty or ill-typed messageId, `accept` means it decodes and the id comes back identical. A case with `wireHex` carries the whole frame in MessagePack hex, for an id a language string cannot hold: the lone surrogate U+D800 is not valid UTF-8, so the vector's messageId is a MessagePack str whose bytes are ED A0 80, and Rust, C#, Kotlin and Python build the frame from those bytes and must refuse it. Letters, numbers and Default_Ignorable are those of Unicode 16.0 in every runtime, from embedded tables (no platform category lookup), so a runtime's own Unicode version cannot change a result. Scope: write_admitted only; error.v1 is untouched.

scenarios.semantics: Each scenario replays events in atMs order against a client that sent each write at its send event; a tick advances the clock without a frame. An event is atMs plus exactly one of: send (a write goes out), frame (a decoded frame arrives), transportAck (delivery, never an answer; the tracker has no input for it), tick (the clock advances), sendFailed (the client's own send of that write failed), sessionEnd (the session ended). Any other key is a defect in the vectors or the runner. A window ends when a write's age reaches it, so an event at exactly sentAt+window finds the write already unconfirmed. 'window' names the constant in vectors.constants that applies (server receipt -> RECEIPT_RESULT_WINDOW_MS, legacy -> LEGACY_RESULT_WINDOW_MS); a tick at or after the window settles unanswered writes as unconfirmed. expect gives the outcome the caller was told per write id; recorded, when present, is the write handle's later state. admitted/refused/unconfirmed are three distinct results; no scenario may settle admitted without a write_admitted frame carrying the write's id.

cases.name: receipt_admits
cases.description: A receipt with the id completes the write as admitted.

cases.name: receipt_before_transport_ack
cases.description: Order against the transport ack is irrelevant.

cases.name: refusal_after_ack
cases.description: A typed refusal after the transport ack refuses; the ack was not admission.

cases.name: refusal_before_ack
cases.description: A typed refusal before the transport ack refuses.

cases.name: ack_only_window_ends_unconfirmed
cases.description: The legacy fallback: an acked write that nothing answered ends unconfirmed, never admitted.

cases.name: window_runs_from_send_not_from_ack
cases.description: A late transport ack does not extend the window.

cases.name: silent_receipt_capable_server_is_unconfirmed_too
cases.description: A server that advertised receipts and stayed silent is still only unconfirmed, and the client reports the fault.

cases.name: legacy_error_with_one_write_in_flight_refuses
cases.description: A pre-receipt server answers with error.v0 and no id: attributable only because one write is unanswered.

cases.name: legacy_error_with_two_writes_in_flight_is_unattributed
cases.description: An id-less error with two unanswered writes names neither: both stay pending and end unconfirmed.

cases.name: batch_names_the_refused_member
cases.description: A batch is independent writes. The refusal names its member; the others keep their own outcomes.

cases.name: batch_with_one_member_unanswered
cases.description: A member nothing answered is unconfirmed; the batch as a whole is admitted only if every member is.

cases.name: session_ends_before_an_answer
cases.description: A lost session leaves unanswered writes unconfirmed, not failed and not admitted.

cases.name: late_refusal_is_recorded_not_told
cases.description: An answer after the window does not change what the caller was told; the handle records refused_late.

cases.name: duplicate_resend_of_an_admitted_write_is_admitted_again
cases.description: The server answers a re-sent admitted messageId with the receipt again, never an error.

cases.name: an_answer_for_an_unknown_id_is_ignored
cases.description: A frame naming no write in flight settles nothing.

cases.name: late_receipt_is_recorded_admitted_late
cases.description: A receipt after the window: the caller was told unconfirmed, the handle records admitted_late; a caller must consult it before resending.

cases.name: receipt_inside_the_receipt_window_is_not_late
cases.description: The receipt-capable window is 5 s: a receipt at 1.2 s admits.

cases.name: legacy_window_is_not_used_against_a_receipt_server
cases.description: At 500 ms a receipt-capable server's write is still pending, not unconfirmed.

cases.name: error_v1_without_id_with_one_write_in_flight_refuses
cases.description: An error.v1 whose messageId is nil names no write: like error.v0 it is attributable only because one write is unanswered.

cases.name: error_v1_without_id_with_two_writes_in_flight_is_unattributed
cases.description: An error.v1 with a nil messageId settles neither of two unanswered writes; each ends unconfirmed at its window.

cases.name: send_failed_is_unconfirmed_and_touches_no_other_write
cases.description: The client's own send of w1 failed: w1 is unconfirmed local_send_failed, never refused; w2 is unaffected and settles on its own receipt.

cases.name: error_without_id_after_the_window_settles_nothing
cases.description: Once w1 is unconfirmed no write is unanswered, so an error that names no write is attributed to nothing and records nothing on w1.

cases.name: receipt_one_millisecond_inside_the_window_admits
cases.description: A receipt 1 ms before the window ends settles the write admitted.

cases.name: receipt_at_the_exact_window_boundary_is_late
cases.description: The window ends when the write's age reaches it: a receipt at exactly that instant finds w1 already unconfirmed and is recorded admitted_late.

cases.name: send_after_session_end_is_unconfirmed_at_once
cases.description: A write registered after the session ended can never be answered: it settles unconfirmed session_ended when sent, and the earlier write keeps its own receipt.

counts.semantics: How many of each a runner must have run. A runner that reads fewer (a parser that drops entries, a loop over nothing) fails instead of passing quietly; a runner that meets an event key outside scenarios.semantics fails too.

contentHash.definition: sha256(msgpack([operation, schemaId, recordKey, payload])), payload a msgpack bin for a put and nil for a delete; hex lowercase

dedupe.semantics: Replay writes in order against a receipt-capable server whose actors are transport-authenticated. expect lists the answer per write in order and how many times a write was applied to the store in total. 'invalid' means error.v1 message_invalid with details.field messageId and the write's id.
